readme: The noun that goes with a COUNT. FriendlyAmt (pipeline\build-v2-spec.ps1) renders a whole-item
amount from densities.json's 'each' weight, and until 2026-08-04 it returned the bare number:
'Potato (generic): 18.4 (3909 g)'. Every one of its nine sibling branches appends a unit (' lb',
' cups', ' cans', ' large eggs', ' oz'); the each branch was the only one that forgot. 661 lines
across 339 of the 513 specs shipped that way.
WHY THIS IS A CURATED FILE AND NOT DERIVED FROM densities.json. The 'each' key is overloaded: for
produce it means one whole item, but for several liquids it is a cup by another name (Chicken Broth
each = 240 g IS a cup). cook-measure-lib.ps1 hit exactly this and dropped 'each' from CM_PREF rather
than invent a noun for it (see its header: 'a number with no noun and no meaning'). So the noun has
to be stated per item by someone who knows the food. An item that reaches the each branch without an
entry here is a BUILD ERROR, not a silent bare number - that throw is what keeps this fixed.
'one' is used at exactly 1, 'many' otherwise, including fractions ('0.7 apples', '1.5 onions') - the
count is a real fraction of a whole item and the gram figure beside it carries the precision. The
counts are NOT rounded: ingredients_display, scaler.ing[].buy, cost_lines and the JSON-LD
head.recipeIngredient all state the same quantity, and rounding one of the four desynchronises them.

notes.Bay Leaves: densities each = 0.6 g, and every shipped line is a single leaf at 1 g.
notes.Celery: a stalk (rib), not the whole bunch - densities stalk = each = 55 g. The cost section buys the bunch.
notes.Green Cabbage: 'heads' matches the purchase unit the receipt already prints ('Buy 2 heads') and the writers' own JSON-LD ('1.7 heads green cabbage'). densities carries head = each = 900 g.
notes.Japanese Curry Roux: the writers' JSON-LD says '7 boxes' and the receipt says 'Buy 7 3.2oz boxs'. densities gained box = 92 AND boxes = 92: 'boxes' is a CM_PKGWORD, so repair-cook-measures treats it as guilty until it can weigh it, and its singulariser only strips a trailing 's' ('boxes' -> 'boxe'), so the plural key has to be there too or the label gets rewritten to a weight on the next repair pass.
notes.Lemon Juice: the count is lemons, not bottles - the brand paren is ReaLemon, so the label reads '3 lemons worth (141 g)', which is the writers' own JSON-LD wording ('3 lemons worth of lemon juice').
notes.Orange Juice: same shape as Lemon Juice; JSON-LD says '5 oranges worth of orange juice' and the receipt buys a 52floz carton.
notes.Zucchini: 'zucchinis' is the catalog's own plural - all 5 lines that already carried a unit use it.
